column1: # IT terms of the TermProtector experiment (DR-07 §15). One term per line, tab separated:
# canonical<TAB>aliases (comma separated)<TAB>flag<TAB>directions to protect<TAB>spellings to normalize
# Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries. Aliases are other spellings of the same name (NodeJS -> Node.js);
# different names (HTML5, K8s) are their own lines. Columns 4 and 5 are written by tools/mt/term_risk.py --write:
# - directions to protect: the model breaks the term even when spelled canonically, so it is replaced by a
#   placeholder (TERM1...) for that direction and put back exactly as typed afterwards;
# - spellings to normalize ("lower@vi_to_en", "cap@en_to_vi"): the model breaks that all-lowercase or Capitalized
#   spelling but keeps the canonical one, so it is rewritten canonically (Javascript -> JavaScript);
# - anything else stays as typed, as do ALL CAPS words and terms inside URLs, domains, paths and file names.
# - flag "en_common": also an ordinary English word (react, rust, windows...): in an English source it is only
#   handled when written exactly as listed and not as the first word.
# After editing: python -I tools/mt/term_risk.py --write. Experiment of DR-07 §15 only: the app does not use this
# list since policy v1 (its runtime lexicon is app/src/main/assets/text/mt_rule_lexicon_v1.json, DR-07 §16).
